_about: Career goals (milestones). The engine scores and schedules these. Term codes: 1F = year 1 fall, 1S = spring, 1U = summer after year 1, … 4S, then G1/G2 = first two terms after graduation. window = earliest term it makes sense, the ideal range, and the latest useful term.

goals.title: Meet a career advisor and sketch a 4-year plan
goals.why: Gets a human in your corner early and surfaces campus programs you'd miss.

goals.title: Complete your Handshake profile
goals.why: Your campus's employers and career fairs run through Handshake.

goals.title: Write your first college resume
goals.why: Nearly every application below needs one.

goals.title: Update and get your resume reviewed
goals.why: A resume goes stale every semester you gain experience.

goals.title: Research 3 careers on O*NET and BLS
goals.why: Know what the jobs involve and pay before you optimize for them.

goals.title: File the FAFSA (every year)
goals.deadline: Before NJ state deadlines in spring; file as early as October
goals.why: Missing it can cost thousands in grants.

goals.title: Check EOF, TAG, Garden State Guarantee, and tuition assistance eligibility
goals.why: Money pressure is the most common reason students skip unpaid or low-paid experience.

goals.title: Write and practice a 30-second introduction
goals.why: You'll use it at every fair, info session, and coffee chat.

goals.title: Write a reusable cover letter template
goals.why: Many internship and fellowship applications still ask for one.

goals.title: Do a mock interview with your career center
goals.why: Interview skill is trainable; most students only practice live.

goals.title: Keep your GPA at or above 3.0
goals.why: Many programs (McNair, co-ops, fellowships, federal internships) screen at 2.5–3.0.

goals.title: Build a complete LinkedIn profile
goals.why: Recruiters search LinkedIn first; it's also how alumni will check you out after a chat.

goals.title: Connect with 50 relevant people (classmates, alumni, speakers)
goals.why: Warm connections turn into referrals, which beat cold applications.

goals.title: Post or engage on LinkedIn monthly (projects, events, wins)
goals.why: Visible work keeps you in recruiters' feeds before you apply.

goals.title: Get a professional headshot and email signature
goals.why: Small polish that makes every profile and email look intentional.

goals.title: Set up GitHub with a profile README
goals.why: Tech hiring managers often check GitHub before the resume.

goals.title: Commit code consistently for a semester (3+ days a week)
goals.why: A steady contribution graph signals real, ongoing practice.

goals.title: Get your first pull request merged into an open-source project
goals.why: Proves you can read someone else's code and work through review.

goals.title: Publish a portfolio site with 3 projects
goals.why: A link that shows your work does more than a bullet that describes it.

goals.title: Build a portfolio of 3–5 published writing samples
goals.why: Communication, policy, and PR employers ask for clips or writing samples.

goals.title: Publish a Kaggle notebook or finish a competition
goals.why: A public analysis is concrete proof of data skills.

goals.title: Create an ORCID iD and list your posters and papers
goals.why: Grad programs and journals expect a research identity.

goals.title: Learn core Excel (lookups, pivots, charts)
goals.why: Shows up in most business, health, and policy roles.

goals.title: Build a three-statement financial model
goals.why: Standard technical screen for finance internships.

goals.title: Learn Python basics
goals.why: The most transferable programming language across fields.

goals.title: Learn SQL
goals.why: Most analyst postings list SQL.

goals.title: Build a dashboard in Tableau or Power BI
goals.why: Turning data into a clear picture is what gets analysts noticed.

goals.title: Learn R or SPSS for statistics
goals.why: Research labs and public health jobs run on statistical software.

goals.title: Solve 100 data structures and algorithms problems
goals.why: Coding interviews for software roles still test this.

goals.title: Use Git and GitHub for every project
goals.why: Version control is assumed on day one of any tech job.

goals.title: Get proficient in CAD (SOLIDWORKS or Onshape)
goals.why: Mechanical and device design postings list CAD first.

goals.title: Learn MATLAB
goals.why: Common in engineering coursework and R&D roles.

goals.title: Learn Figma and design one app flow
goals.why: The standard tool for UX and product design portfolios.

goals.title: Earn Google Ads/Analytics and HubSpot certifications
goals.why: Free, fast, and listed in entry-level digital marketing postings.

goals.title: Give 3 presentations outside class (club, Toastmasters, symposium)
goals.why: Presentation skill is one of the top things employers ask for.

goals.title: Write a memo or policy brief and get feedback
goals.why: Clear short writing is a daily skill in policy, business, and health jobs.

goals.title: Reach conversational level in a second language
goals.why: Valued in public service, healthcare, and international business.

goals.title: Learn core lab techniques in a research lab
goals.why: Lab skills on a resume are what get industry and research offers.

goals.title: Complete 20 hands-on security labs or a CTF
goals.why: Security hiring rewards hands-on proof over coursework.

goals.title: Complete Bloomberg Market Concepts
goals.why: Common talking point and resume line in finance interviews.

goals.title: Join 1–2 organizations tied to your field
goals.why: The easiest source of peers, mentors, and leadership roles.

goals.title: Take an officer or project-lead role
goals.why: Leadership is one of the strongest signals on an early-career resume.

goals.title: Hold a part-time or campus job
goals.why: Any job builds reliability, and many students need the income.

goals.title: Volunteer with a community organization
goals.why: Builds perspective and stories for interviews; required for some health paths.

goals.title: Work as a research assistant with a professor
goals.why: Opens recommendation letters and research summers.

goals.title: Do a paid summer research program
goals.why: The core experience for PhD and research-industry paths.

goals.title: Complete an honors thesis or independent research project
goals.why: Top signal for grad school and research careers.

goals.title: Build and ship a personal project
goals.why: Something you built is the best answer to 'tell me about a project.'

goals.title: Compete in a hackathon
goals.why: Fast team experience and recruiter exposure in a weekend.

goals.title: Join an engineering design team (Formula SAE, robotics, etc.)
goals.why: Hands-on build experience that engineering recruiters ask about first.

goals.title: Compete in a case competition
goals.why: Shows business problem-solving under pressure; firms recruit at them.

goals.title: Complete 2 virtual job simulations
goals.why: A quick way to test a field and get interview stories before your first internship.

goals.title: Do a first internship or career-related summer job
goals.why: Any relevant summer experience makes the junior-year internship far easier to land.

goals.title: Do an internship in your target field
goals.why: Junior-summer internships are the main pipeline to full-time offers.

goals.title: Complete a 6-month co-op
goals.why: Deeper than an internship and often converts to a job offer.

goals.title: Shadow professionals for 40+ hours
goals.why: Health programs want proof you know what the job is.

goals.title: Log 150+ hours of patient-care experience
goals.why: Medical, PA, and PT schools screen on hands-on patient care.

goals.title: Complete a nursing externship
goals.why: Hospitals often hire new grads from their own extern pools.

goals.title: Work as a licensed pharmacy intern
goals.why: Paid experience that also builds residency and job references.

goals.title: Complete your BSW field placement
goals.why: Required for the degree and for advanced-standing MSW programs.

goals.title: Produce work for student media (newspaper, radio, or TV)
goals.why: Published work is the entry ticket for media and PR roles.

goals.title: Intern in a government or campaign office
goals.why: Public-sector jobs hire from people they already know.

goals.title: Observe court, do a ride-along, or volunteer in reentry
goals.why: Shows you understand the system you want to work in.

goals.title: Study or intern abroad
goals.why: Builds independence and global perspective; Gilman covers costs for Pell recipients.

goals.title: Pitch a venture or join a startup
goals.why: Teaches selling an idea and moving fast.

goals.title: Tutor or work as a teaching assistant
goals.why: Teaching proves mastery and builds faculty relationships.

goals.title: Attend your first career fair (to look, not to land)
goals.why: Low-pressure practice before the fairs that count.

goals.title: Work a career fair with a target list of employers
goals.why: Fall junior-year fairs feed most junior-summer internships.

goals.title: Do 5 informational interviews with alumni
goals.why: The fastest way to learn what a job is really like and get referred.

goals.title: Build relationships with 2 professors (office hours, research)
goals.why: You'll need recommendation letters for research, fellowships, and grad school.

goals.title: Find a mentor in your target field
goals.why: A mentor shortens every decision on this map.

goals.title: Join a professional society as a student member
goals.why: Student rates are cheap and give access to scholarships, job boards, and conferences.

goals.title: Attend a national conference or diversity career conference
goals.why: Conference career fairs often interview on the spot.

goals.title: Attend 3 employer info sessions
goals.why: Recruiters remember the people who showed up.

goals.title: Get CPR/BLS certified
goals.why: Required for nearly every clinical job and volunteer role.

goals.title: Earn EMT certification
goals.why: Fastest route to paid patient-care hours.

goals.title: Earn the RBT credential
goals.why: Common paid clinical job for psychology students.

goals.title: Become a certified pharmacy technician
goals.why: Paid pharmacy experience while in school.

goals.title: Earn the aPHR
goals.why: Entry-level HR certification with no experience requirement.

goals.title: Sit for the CHES exam
goals.why: Recognized credential for health education roles.

goals.title: Earn ACSM or NSCA certification
goals.why: Required for many fitness and strength roles.

goals.title: Earn CompTIA Security+ or ISC2 CC
goals.why: Baseline credential for security and many government IT jobs.

goals.title: Earn an entry cloud certification (AWS Cloud Practitioner)
goals.why: Cloud shows up in most modern software and IT roles.

goals.title: Complete a Google Career Certificate
goals.why: Structured, recognized skill credential in data, IT, UX, or project management.

goals.title: Earn the SOLIDWORKS CSWA
goals.why: Proves CAD skill on paper.

goals.title: Take the FE exam
goals.why: First step to a PE license; easiest while coursework is fresh.

goals.title: Earn a Lean Six Sigma Green Belt
goals.why: Valued in manufacturing and operations roles.

goals.title: Earn Microsoft Office Specialist: Excel
goals.why: Turns 'proficient in Excel' into something verifiable.

goals.title: Complete CITI human-subjects training
goals.why: Required before joining most human-subjects labs.

goals.title: Plan your path to 150 credit hours for the CPA
goals.why: NJ requires 150 credits; deciding early saves a year or a lot of money.

goals.title: Add a minor or certificate that fills a gap (data, writing, a language)
goals.why: A targeted minor can cover what your major doesn't.

goals.title: Apply to the Eagleton Undergraduate Associates program
goals.why: Selective politics program with a stipend and placement network.

goals.title: Meet your campus fellowships office
goals.why: Many awards need a campus nomination a year ahead.

goals.title: Apply for a national fellowship (Goldwater, Truman, Fulbright, Gilman)
goals.why: Even unsuccessful applications sharpen your story for everything else.

goals.title: Prep for your entrance exam (MCAT, LSAT, GRE, PCAT)
goals.why: Gate for professional and graduate school.

goals.title: Line up 3 recommendation letters
goals.why: Letter writers need months of notice and real knowledge of your work.

goals.title: Build a balanced list of grad or professional programs
goals.why: A balanced list beats applying only to reach schools.

goals.title: Draft and revise your personal statement
goals.why: Takes several drafts; start before senior fall.

goals.title: Prepare for the NCLEX-RN
goals.why: Licensure gate after graduation.

goals.title: Decide on residency vs. industry vs. community practice
goals.why: Each route has different deadlines and experiences to build.

goals.title: Apply to 5 outside scholarships
goals.why: Free money; many awards get few applicants.

goals.title: Apply to first- and second-year programs (SEO, MLT, INROADS, early-ID)
goals.why: These programs feed directly into the competitive junior internships.

goals.title: Apply to summer research programs (REUs, RISE, SURE)
goals.why: Deadlines come months before summer.

goals.title: Apply to 15+ summer opportunities for after sophomore year
goals.deadline: Most summer roles fill by March
goals.why: Sophomore summer experience is what makes junior internships winnable.

goals.title: Apply to 30+ target internships for junior summer
goals.deadline: Many large employers recruit August–October of junior year
goals.why: The main recruiting window for full-time offers.

goals.title: Apply to federal internships on USAJOBS
goals.why: Federal hiring uses its own resume rules and timelines.

goals.title: Run your full-time job search (or convert a return offer)
goals.why: Start in senior fall; many offers go out before spring.

goals.title: Submit graduate or professional school applications
goals.why: Most deadlines fall between September and January of senior year.

goals.title: Compare and negotiate your offer
goals.why: Many entry-level offers have room to negotiate; few graduates ask.

goals.title: Enter a student packaging design competition
goals.why: A finished package design is the portfolio piece packaging recruiters ask about.

goals.title: Add the Rutgers packaging certificate
goals.why: Four packaging courses open packaging and consumer-products roles to engineers in other majors.
